doc: Internal transitions (a state's `internal` list; also called static reactions): no exit or entry, substates keep their configuration, selected and conflict-checked like a transition from the state to itself, after the state's outgoing transitions.

steps.doc: A's and B's internal transitions fire together (orthogonal regions); P's is dropped: a transition taken inside P beats P's own, as for any ancestor.
A's internal transition is taken first, so P -> Q, which would exit A, is dropped.
An internal transition's signal is handled by another internal transition.
A -> A2 and B's internal transition in one microstep: exit, actions, entry.
P keeps its configuration: a transition from P to itself would re-enter A.
A2 has no eBoth; B's internal transition still beats P's.
Nothing inside P reacts, so P -> Q fires.
P -eOrder[go]-> Q is tried first; its guard fails, so P's internal transition fires.
A state's outgoing transitions come before its internal ones.
